mainTopic: The end of the רבי עקיבא story and related stories about wives and Torah learning, then the משנה and גמרא about a מורדת: what a rebelling spouse refuses and how the כתובה is adjusted.
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of רבי עקיבא. He learns for twenty-four years, comes home with 24,000 students, and declares that all their Torah belongs to his wife. Her father, כלבא שבוע, has his vow cancelled and gives רבי עקיבא half his money, and רבי עקיבא's daughter does the same for בן עזאי. The גמרא then tells of רב יוסף בריה דרבא, who tried to leave his learning early to visit home on ערב יום כפור. A new משנה follows: a wife who rebels has her כתובה reduced every week, and a husband who rebels has his wife's כתובה increased every week. In the גמרא, רב הונא says the wife's rebellion means refusing relations, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says it means refusing household work. Each view is challenged, the 'work' view from the rebelling husband and the 'relations' view from a ברייתא about a נדה, and each is defended. The amud ends as a second version of the ברייתא challenge, about a sick woman, begins to turn against the 'work' view. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wife answers an old man's taunt and רבי עקיבא stays twelve more years
steps.stepSummary: After hearing an old man mock her as a 'living widow,' רבי עקיבא's wife says she would gladly have him learn twelve more years. רבי עקיבא takes this as permission and goes back to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Are you living like a widow while your husband is alive?!' She said to him: 'If he would listen to me, he would sit and learn another twelve years.' רבי עקיבא said: 'I am doing this with permission.' He went back and sat another twelve years in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רבי עקיבא continues from the previous daf. His wife answers a man who mocked her for living alone, and רבי עקיבא, overhearing, goes back to learn another twelve years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her answer shows she is fully behind his learning, even though she is suffering. רבי עקיבא does not stay away on his own decision. He goes back only because her words give him clear permission.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a 'widow' while the husband is alive (living alone while he is away)

phrases.english: Are you living as a widow while your husband is alive?!
phrases.notes: These are the last words of an old man mocking her. His taunt begins on the previous daf.

phrases.english: She said to him: If he would listen to me,
he would sit another twelve years.
phrases.notes: The ending in square brackets is the corrected spelling of the word 'another'.

phrases.english: He said: I am doing this with permission.
He went back and sat

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי אַחְרָינְיָי[תָא] בְּבֵי רַב.
phrases.english: another twelve years in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי עקיבא story from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's wife willingly gives up more years with him so he can learn, and he treats her words as permission.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא returns and honors his wife in front of everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא comes home with 24,000 students. His wife goes out in her poor clothes, falls at his feet, and when his attendants push her away, he says all their Torah is really hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came back, he brought 24,000 students with him. His wife heard and went out to greet him. Her neighbors said: 'Borrow nice clothes and dress up.' She answered: 'A righteous man knows the soul of his animal.' When she reached him, she fell on her face and kissed his feet. His attendants tried to push her away. He said to them: 'Leave her! My Torah and your Torah are really hers.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא comes home as a great teacher. He publicly declares that his wife deserves the credit for all the Torah he and his students have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She refuses to borrow fancy clothes and quotes a פסוק meaning that a righteous person recognizes those who depend on him, so he will know her. The students do not know who she is. רבי עקיבא's words teach that the one who makes Torah learning possible shares fully in that Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous man knows the soul of his animal (משלי 12:10)

steps.whyThisMatters: This line, 'mine and yours is hers,' is the classic source that a wife who supports her husband's learning shares in his Torah.

phrases.english: When he came, he brought with him
twenty-four thousand students.
His wife heard,
and she was going out to greet him.
Her neighbors said to her:
Borrow some clothes and dress yourself.
She said to them: 'A righteous man knows the soul of his animal.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָטְיָא לְגַבֵּיהּ, נְפַלָה עַל אַפַּהּ,
phrases.english: When she reached him, she fell on her face,
and was kissing his feet.
His attendants were pushing her away.
He said to them: Leave her,
what is mine and what is yours is hers.
phrases.notes: He means the Torah that he and his students learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא אַיְיתִי בַּהֲדֵיהּ עֶשְׂרִין וְאַרְבְּעָה אַלְפֵי תַּלְמִידֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story continues: he finishes the second twelve years and comes home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah learned by רבי עקיבא and his students is credited to his wife.

steps.title: Her father's vow is annulled and he gives half his wealth
steps.stepSummary: כלבא שבוע, the wife's father, comes to the great sage hoping to have his vow annulled. רבי עקיבא annuls it by showing the vow was made by mistake, and then reveals who he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her father heard that a great man had come to town. He said: 'I will go to him. Maybe he can cancel my vow.' He came, and רבי עקיבא asked him: 'When you made the vow, did you think he would become a great man?' He answered: 'If I had thought he would know even one chapter, even one הלכה, I never would have vowed.' רבי עקיבא said: 'I am that man.' The father fell on his face, kissed his feet, and gave him half of his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The father, who had vowed that his daughter would get nothing from him, asks the visiting sage to cancel his vow. The sage turns out to be his own son-in-law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow can be cancelled if it was based on a mistaken assumption. The father vowed only because he thought עקיבא was an ignorant man. Since that turned out to be false, the vow falls away, and the father happily gives half his wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man (a great Torah scholar)
With the thought that, on the assumption that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the principle that a vow made on a false assumption can be undone.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע אֲבוּהָ דַּאֲתָא גַּבְרָא רַבָּה לְמָתָא,
phrases.english: Her father heard that a great man had come to town.
He said: I will go to him,
perhaps he will annul my vow.
phrases.notes: This is the vow from the previous daf, where he swore his daughter would get no benefit from his property.

phrases.english: He came to him, and he said to him:
Did you make the vow thinking he would become a great man?
He said to him: Even one chapter,
phrases.notes: He means: had I thought he would know even this little, I would never have vowed.

phrases.english: or even one הלכה.
He said to him: I am he.

phrases.aramaic: נְפַל עַל אַפֵּיהּ וְנַשְּׁקֵיהּ עַל כַּרְעֵיהּ
phrases.english: He fell on his face and kissed his feet,
and gave him half of his money.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע אֲבוּהָ דַּאֲתָא גַּבְרָא רַבָּה לְמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the wife to her father and resolves his vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father's vow is cancelled because it rested on a false assumption, and he rewards רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The daughter follows in her mother's footsteps
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's daughter did the same thing for בן עזאי, and the גמרא connects this to a popular saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא's daughter did the same for בן עזאי. This is what people say: 'A ewe follows a ewe; as the mother acts, so the daughter acts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the רבי עקיבא story by adding that his daughter also married a man and sent him away to learn, just as her mother had done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that this kind of devotion can be passed down from mother to daughter. The folk saying sums up the whole story.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבי עקיבא story teaches that a wife who sacrifices for her husband's Torah owns a share of it, and that this path was continued by their daughter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva's daughter
did the same for Ben Azzai.
And this is what people say:
A ewe follows after a ewe;
as the mother's deeds, so are the daughter's deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing parallel story and a saying that sums it up.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A daughter copies her mother's devotion to her husband's Torah.

steps.title: רב יוסף son of רבא leaves his learning early and meets his angry father
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרבא was sent to learn for six years but tried to visit home after three, on ערב יום כפור. His father came out armed and rebuked him, and in the argument neither of them ate the meal before the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sent his son, רב יוסף, to the study hall to learn from רב יוסף. They set six years for him. After three years, when ערב יום כפור arrived, he said: 'I will go and see my family.' His father heard, took a weapon, and went out to meet him. He said to him: 'You remembered your mistress?' Some say he said: 'You remembered your dove?' They got caught up in the argument, and neither one ate the meal before the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story about a husband away learning, this time one where the husband tried to come home too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story balances the רבי עקיבא story. Here the father strongly objects to the son breaking off his learning early. The two versions differ in how harshly he spoke: 'mistress' is a sharp insult, while 'dove' is a softer word for a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: They set for him (an agreed period)
Ate the סעודה מפסקת (the last meal before the fast)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named רב יוסף here: the student (רבא's son) and his teacher, the great רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rava,
his father sent him to the study hall
to learn before Rav Yosef.
They set six years for him.
When three years had passed,
the eve of Yom Kippur arrived.
He said: I will go and see the members of my household.
His father heard,
took a weapon, and went out to meet him.
He said to him: You remembered your mistress?
Some say he said to him:
You remembered your dove?
They got caught up in the argument.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מָר אִיפְּסִיק, וְלָא מָר אִיפְּסִיק.
phrases.english: This master did not eat the pre-fast meal, and that master did not eat the pre-fast meal either.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא שַׁדְּרֵיהּ אֲבוּהִי לְבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of husbands leaving home to learn Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא strongly opposed his son cutting short his agreed years of learning.

steps.title: משנה: a rebelling wife's כתובה is reduced each week
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a wife who rebels against her husband loses seven דינרים from her כתובה each week. רבי יהודה says the amount is seven טרפעיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who rebels against her husband: we reduce her כתובה by seven דינרים each week. רבי יהודה says: seven טרפעיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about a wife who rebels in the marriage. Her כתובה is cut by a set amount every week as a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty presses her to end the rebellion, since every week costs her money. רבי יהודה agrees there is a weekly fine but holds it is smaller: half-dinar coins instead of full דינרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who rebels against her husband
The marriage contract and the money promised to the wife in it

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who rebels against her husband:
we reduce her ketubah
by seven dinars each week.
Rabbi Yehuda says: seven terapa'ikin.
phrases.notes: A טרפעיק is worth half a דינר, so he makes the fine half as large.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹרֶדֶת עַל בַּעְלָהּ פּוֹחֲתִין לָהּ מִכְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new legal topic. The stories have ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rebelling wife's כתובה is reduced weekly: seven דינרים according to the תנא קמא, seven טרפעיקין according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: משנה: how long the reduction continues
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the reductions continue until the whole כתובה is used up. רבי יוסי says they keep going even beyond that, so the husband can collect from any inheritance she later receives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when does he keep reducing? Until the full value of her כתובה. רבי יוסי says: he keeps reducing forever, so that if she later inherits money from somewhere else, he collects from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks how far the penalty goes. It brings two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first opinion, the fine stops once the כתובה reaches zero. רבי יוסי holds that the fine keeps building up as a debt she owes, which he can collect from other money she gets later, such as an inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to the amount of her כתובה

phrases.english: Until when does he reduce?
Until it equals her ketubah.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם הוּא פּוֹחֵת וְהוֹלֵךְ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: He can always keep on reducing,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁאִם תִּפּוֹל לָהּ יְרוּשָּׁה מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: so that if she receives an inheritance from another source,
he collects from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the penalty introduced in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא stops the fine at the value of the כתובה. רבי יוסי lets it continue and be collected from her other assets.

steps.title: משנה: a rebelling husband has his wife's כתובה increased
steps.stepSummary: In the opposite case, a husband who rebels against his wife has three דינרים added to her כתובה each week. רבי יהודה says three טרפעיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, a man who rebels against his wife: we add three דינרים a week to her כתובה. רבי יהודה says: three טרפעיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the matching rule for a husband who rebels. Instead of a reduction, her כתובה grows each week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty works in both directions, so either spouse who refuses marital duties is fined. The husband's weekly amount is three, smaller than the wife's seven. רבי יהודה again holds the coins are half-dinars.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who rebels against his wife

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה fines a rebelling spouse every week: the wife's כתובה goes down by seven, and the rebelling husband's obligation goes up by three. רבי יהודה measures both in half-dinars.

phrases.english: And similarly, a man who rebels against his wife:
we add to her ketubah
three dinars each week.
Rabbi Yehuda says: three terapa'ikin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the parallel case of a rebelling husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rebelling husband has three דינרים added to his wife's כתובה each week; רבי יהודה says three טרפעיקין.

steps.title: What exactly is the wife rebelling against?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what kind of refusal makes a woman a מורדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A rebelling wife: what is she rebelling against?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by asking a basic question. What exactly is the wife refusing to do? This sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a penalty of seven דינרים a week but never said what counts as 'rebelling.' The גמרא needs a definition before it can apply the penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who 'rebels,' meaning she refuses something she owes her husband

phrases.english: GEMARA: A rebelling wife: from what is she rebelling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in steps 6–8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of refusal makes a wife a מורדת?

steps.title: Two answers: marital relations or household work
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says she refuses marital relations. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says she refuses household work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: she refuses marital relations. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: she refuses household work.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to the question. Is the rebellion about intimacy or about the household jobs she owes him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers are a refusal of something the wife owes her husband, but they are very different kinds of duties. The rest of this section tests each view against earlier sources.

keyTerms.meaning: The household work a wife does for her husband

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא = refusing relations. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא = refusing work. Keep these two views straight, because every challenge that follows targets one of them.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: from marital relations.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מִמְּלָאכָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: from work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either refusal of relations (רב הונא) or refusal of household work (רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

steps.title: Challenge from the rebelling husband
steps.stepSummary: The משנה also speaks of a husband who rebels. That fits 'relations,' but a husband doesn't owe his wife household work.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'And likewise a husband who rebels against his wife.' This works for the one who says the rebellion is about relations. But for the one who says it's about work, does the husband owe her work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. If rebelling means refusing work, the משנה's case of a rebelling husband makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations is a two-way duty, so a husband can also refuse it. But household work is the wife's duty, so how could a husband 'rebel' by refusing it?

phrases.english: We learned: And likewise one who rebels against his wife.
Granted, according to the one who says from relations, fine.
But according to the one who says from work,
is he obligated to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'work' opinion from step 10 against the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה applies rebellion to a husband too. A husband owes no household work, so 'work' cannot be the meaning.

steps.title: The husband refuses to support her
steps.stepSummary: Yes, a husband has duties too. The husband's rebellion is refusing to feed and support his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it's talking about a husband who says, 'I will not feed her and I will not support her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. A husband's version of 'refusing work' is refusing to provide for his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side has a practical duty. She does household work and he provides food and support. So 'rebellion' means refusing your own practical duty, which works for both spouses.

phrases.english: Yes, in one who says: 'I will not feed and I will not support.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, בְּאוֹמֵר אֵינִי זָן וְאֵינִי מְפַרְנֵס
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A husband owes no 'work,' so he can't rebel in that sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rebellion is refusing to feed and support her, which is his practical duty.

steps.title: But רב says such a husband must divorce right away
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a husband who refuses to support must divorce her and pay the כתובה. So why would weekly additions apply?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: One who says 'I will not feed and will not support' must divorce her and give her the כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 12. According to רב, that husband is forced to divorce at once, so there's no room for a slow weekly penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds three דינרים each week, which assumes the marriage carries on for a while. רב's rule seems to end the marriage immediately, so it clashes with that picture.

keyTerms.meaning: He must divorce her and pay the כתובה

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
One who says: 'I will not feed and I will not support'
must divorce and give the כתובה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the husband's rebellion is refusing support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב requires immediate divorce for that husband, which leaves no time for weekly additions to the כתובה.

steps.title: First the court tries to talk to him
steps.stepSummary: Before forcing a divorce, the court consults with him. During that time the weekly additions apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And don't we first need to consult with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the divorce isn't instant. There is a period of talking with the husband first, and the weekly penalty runs during that period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule tells us where things end if the husband refuses to change. The משנה's weekly addition covers the time in between, while he is still being urged to reconsider.

keyTerms.meaning: To consult with him, to see if he'll change his mind

steps.whatToRemember: The 'work' view survives. A husband 'rebels' by refusing support, and the weekly additions apply while the court is still talking to him, before any forced divorce.

phrases.english: And isn't it necessary to consult with him?
phrases.notes: While the court is trying to get him to change his mind, the three דינרים a week keep adding up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the two rules apply at different stages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's rule means divorce right away, so weekly penalties are impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a consultation period first, and the weekly additions apply during it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: even a נדה can be a מורדת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that applies the rule of מורדת to many women, including a נדה, a sick woman and a שומרת יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: It's all the same to me: a betrothed woman, a married woman, even a נדה, even a sick woman, even a woman waiting for her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the start of a new challenge. The next step will explain which opinion it seems to contradict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the rule of מורדת applies even to women who cannot have relations right now, like a נדה. This sets up a problem for רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)
It's the same to me (the same law applies)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A woman in her menstrual period, forbidden to her husband
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
It is the same to me: a betrothed woman, or a married woman,
and even a menstruating woman, and even a sick woman,
and even a woman waiting for her yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge, this time aimed at the other opinion from step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes women who are forbidden or unable to have relations anyway.

steps.title: How can a נדה refuse relations?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא fits the 'work' view. But under the 'relations' view, a נדה is forbidden anyway, so her refusal shouldn't matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for the one who says the rebellion is about work, that's fine. But for the one who says it's about relations: is a נדה available for relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא is a problem for רב הונא. A נדה can't have relations right now, so how can she be punished for refusing them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה can still do household work, so the ברייתא fits רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא easily. Under רב הונא, though, her refusal seems to take nothing away from her husband.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says from work, it is fine.
But according to the one who says from relations,
is a menstruating woman fit for relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge set up by the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נדה is forbidden to her husband anyway, so refusing relations takes nothing from him. Yet the ברייתא still calls her a מורדת.

steps.title: Bread in the basket
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that knowing she will be available later is very different from knowing she refuses. So her refusal hurts him even now.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: Someone who has bread in his basket is not like someone who has none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא with a well-known saying. Even when relations are not possible right now, her refusal still causes real distress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who knows food is waiting for him is calm even when he isn't eating. Someone without food feels its lack. In the same way, a husband whose wife has declared she refuses him suffers even during her days as a נדה, so the ברייתא fits רב הונא too.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread in his basket: having something available for later

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, both views survive their challenges. 'Work' fits the husband's case as refusing support, and 'relations' fits a נדה because of 'bread in the basket.' The next step brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) in which the ברייתא is turned against the 'work' view.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say relations with a נדה are allowed. He says her refusal still harms the husband, because it takes away what he could have counted on later.

phrases.english: He could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
phrases.english: One who has bread in his basket is not comparable
to one who does not have.
phrases.notes: He means: a husband who knows his wife will be with him later is calmer than one whose wife has refused him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 on behalf of רב הונא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדה's refusal costs her husband nothing, since relations are forbidden anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her refusal still causes him distress now, like having no bread in the basket, so she counts as a מורדת.

steps.title: Another version: the 'relations' view explains the sick woman
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the challenge, the גמרא says the ברייתא's mention of a חולה fits well with the view that מורדת means refusing relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the challenge went differently: It makes sense according to the one who says מורדת is about refusing relations. That is why the ברייתא mentions a sick woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the question from the ברייתא. This line is a setup: it shows which view fits the ברייתא easily, before attacking the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the trouble was a נדה under the 'relations' view. Here the focus moves to the חולה. A sick woman can't do housework, but she can still refuse relations. So under the 'relations' view it makes sense to call her a מורדת. The challenge to the 'work' view is about to come.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted: opens the half of a question that works fine

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the same challenge from the ברייתא (Step 15), told a different way. In this version, the 'relations' view is the one that fits easily, and the 'work' view is the one in trouble.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Granted, according to the one who says it is from marital relations,
that is why it teaches a sick woman.
phrases.notes: A sick woman can't work, but she can still refuse relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִתַּשְׁמִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the challenge from Steps 15-16. Here the 'relations' view fits, using the case of חולה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a מורדת means refusing work (ממלאכה). This half of the question only sets that up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a חולה a מורדת. That only makes sense if refusing relations counts, because a sick woman can't work anyway. The full attack on the 'work' view comes next.
